title: Generalized Bayes loss updates and temperature calibration

items.title: Generalized Bayes loss update and temperature
items.statement: Defines the fixed-observation loss update G_{w,pi,x}(A)=Z^{-1} int_A exp(-w ell_x) d pi for positive finite Z and fixed w>0.
items.strategy: Define the loss section, temperature, normalizer, and normalized density measure without assuming a data-generating model.

references.title: P. G. Bissiri, C. C. Holmes, and S. G. Walker, A general framework for updating belief distributions, JRSS B 78(5), 2016
references.locator: Sections 1.1–1.2, 2.3, and 3.1–3.4; the complete relevant argument is inspected in the 32-page full-text preprint and compared with the final publisher PDF.

items.title: A countable discrete measurable space is standard Borel
items.statement: If S is nonempty and at most countable, then (S,P(S)) is standard Borel.
items.strategy: Use the discrete metric: it is complete and induces the power-set Borel sigma-algebra, while S itself is an at most countable dense subset.

references.title: David Marker, Descriptive Set Theory, Example 1.2, course notes (Fall 2002)
references.locator: §1, Example 1.2, PDF p. 2: the discrete metric on a countable set is complete and induces the discrete topology.

items.title: A finite-normalizer loss update is a probability measure
items.statement: For every admissible prior, observation, and positive finite normalizer, the generalized Bayes loss update has total mass one and is countably additive.
items.strategy: Construct the measure with density exp(-w ell_x), scale by the positive normalizer, and check its total mass.

items.title: The generalized Bayes loss update uniquely minimizes loss plus KL
items.statement: If w>0, 0<Z_w<infinity, and the Gibbs update has finite absolute loss expectation, it uniquely minimizes w E_nu[ell_x]+D(nu||pi) over probabilities nu absolutely continuous with respect to pi with finite objective terms.
items.strategy: Identify the objective gap with D(nu||G), prove its nonnegativity and equality case directly, and verify the Gibbs law is admissible.

items.title: Fixed-temperature generalized Bayes updates are sequentially coherent
items.statement: For a finite sequence of losses at one fixed positive temperature, if each sequential normalizer is finite positive, repeated updates equal one update using the sum of losses.
items.strategy: Use induction on the number of observations and multiply the successive density factors while tracking the normalizer product.

items.title: Calibrating generalized Bayes temperature
items.statement: Records source-proposed temperature elicitation and calibration methods, and states that the update theorem alone proves neither robust-risk guarantees nor frequentist coverage.
items.strategy: Summarize the source's unit-information, hierarchical, cross-validation, subjective, and confidence-interval matching proposals with their limits.

title: Generalized Bayes loss updates and temperature calibration — Examples

items.title: A measurable loss can have an infinite normalizer
items.statement: On a dyadic prior on the nonnegative integers, the finite loss ell(k)=log(pi({k})) makes every unnormalized posterior atom equal to one, so Z=+infinity and no update is defined.
items.strategy: Construct the proper prior from a geometric series, then compute each unnormalized atom exactly.

references.title: P. G. Bissiri, C. C. Holmes, and S. G. Walker, A general framework for updating belief distributions, JRSS B 78(5), 2016

items.title: A generalized Bayes credible set can have zero coverage
items.statement: A fixed positive temperature and a proper loss update do not by themselves guarantee nominal frequentist coverage for posterior credible sets.
items.strategy: Use a two-state experiment whose loss favors the wrong state: the update gives that state posterior mass above 0.95 while its confidence-set coverage at the true state is zero.

items.title: Rescaling loss changes the effective temperature
items.statement: For a two-point prior, multiplying the loss by c>0 at temperature w gives the same update as retaining the loss and using temperature cw; distinct effective temperatures yield distinct updates for a nonconstant loss.
items.strategy: Compute the two normalized weights and compare their posterior odds.

items.title: The unit-temperature likelihood update is ordinary Bayes in a finite model
items.statement: For a two-state finite model with positive likelihood section, unit-temperature negative log-likelihood loss gives the ordinary posterior, computed directly from the joint probabilities.
items.strategy: Compute the two unnormalized prior-likelihood weights, their finite-positive normalizer, and the conditional probabilities.
